title: Concierge Onboarding Microflow for New Projects
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Design a lightweight 'Concierge' microflow that runs when users create their first project in the Redwood Console. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-success by pre-seeding a minimal dashboard, highlighting rollout controls, and surfacing cost literacy in context (token/cost estimates and expected monthly spend). This ticket covers UX flows, prototype screens, copy, and an initial usability test plan.

Why: Current first-project empty states are too generic — engineers create projects but leave without wiring models, routes, or understanding cost/latency trade-offs. A short in-product guided microflow (3–4 steps) should get users to a working inference route, show a sample dashboard, and leave them confident about rollout/defaults and cost implications.

Scope:
- Microflow entry trigger (first project or opt-in from project settings).
- 3-step guided sequence: (1) Quick route creation with sample prompt + model recommendation; (2) Lightweight rollout preview with recommended canary percentages and failover; (3) Cost snapshot card with token estimate + toggleable optimization tips (batching, quantization suggestions).
- Empty-state templates: seeded dashboard widgets (latency, token burn, success rate) and a 'play' button to run a demo inference.
- In-product education elements: contextual tooltips for rollout knobs, short inline explainers for cost metrics, and a dismissible 'Concierge' badge.
- Prototype assets and copy for handoff, plus acceptance criteria and measurables.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Keep microflow < 90 seconds to complete; prefer progressive disclosure (tooltips + a single modal) rather than a full multi-step tour to avoid onboarding fatigue.
- Use conservative defaults for rollouts (canary 5% -> 20% ramp) to be safe for new users but provide one-click presets for power users.
- Cost card shows 'estimated monthly spend range' with best/worst-case and a 'how we calculated this' tooltip linking to a deeper doc.
- Avoid blocking users: flow is fully skippable and stored in project meta so the console can nudge again later.

Prototype links and artifacts (for reviewers):
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/concierge-onboarding-microflow (prototype v1.2)
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Concierge+Onboarding+Microflow
- Demo branch (frontend prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-prototypes/tree/feature/concierge-onboard

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates the 3-step flow end-to-end with working demo inference and seeded dashboard.
- Copy approved by PM and localization lead.
- Usability script and metrics (task completion, perceived helpfulness) drafted and ready for 5 moderated sessions.
- Engineering sign-off on feasibility for rollout defaults and cost-estimate hooks (ENG owners tagged in dependencies).

Success metrics (post-launch, 30d):
- Increase in projects with a configured route within 7 days from 42% -> 65%.
- Decrease in abandoned first-projects (created but no inference requests) by 35%.
- Net survey rating on helpfulness >= 4.0/5 in the follow-up survey.

Next steps:
1) Design critiques this week (Feb 18–20) with PM and Eng.
2) Iterate prototype based on feedback and finalize copy.
3) Run 5 moderated usability sessions (Feb 24–28).
4) Handoff to ENG for light-weight frontend prototyping (target alpha in console-2025.03).
